# Conditional probability — fragments

For events A and B, if P(B) > 0:
P(A | B) = P(A ∩ B) / P(B).
The condition P(B) > 0 matters because division by zero is undefined.

Example: P(A ∩ B) = 0.12 and P(B) = 0.30, so P(A | B) = 0.40.
This does not state that A and B are independent.
For a discrete probability distribution: p_i ≥ 0 and sum from i=1 to n of p_i = 1.
The notes contain no continuous-density formula.
